transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Thank you for seeing me. Um, I guess I'm here because... well, I've just been feeling a bit off lately. It's probably nothing major, but I just can't seem to shake this heavy mix of fear and guilt. It's like I'm tense all day, just waiting for something else to go wrong. And, um, I keep blaming myself for not stopping what happened. I know that sounds silly, and I'm sure other people deal with much worse, but... does that make sense? Is that something you can help with?
Do you find yourself having repetitive thoughts that you can't stop thinking about?

Um, yeah, I guess so. I mean, everyone gets things stuck in their head sometimes, right? I hope I'm not making too big a deal out of it. But... well, I work as a building inspector, and sometimes I'll just be doing my normal job, like, measuring a railing or... or I'll just hear a ladder scrape on a site. And out of nowhere, I just... I can see my husband falling. 

It's like it's happening right in front of me all over again. My stomach just completely drops, and my hands get all shaky. I try really hard to just push it away and keep working, because I know I shouldn't let it get to me so much, and I definitely don't want to make a scene at work. I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds a bit dramatic... is that the kind of thing you mean?
Are these memories of your husband falling usually triggered by something specific, like the sound of a ladder scraping?

Um, yes, exactly. Like I was just saying, it seems to usually be tied to those normal work things. If I'm up measuring a railing, or... yeah, especially that sound of a ladder scraping against a wall. 

It's almost like a switch flips, and out of nowhere I'm just seeing him fall all over again, like it's happening right in front of me. And then my stomach just drops and I get those shaky hands. I really try to hide it when it happens, because I know it's just a regular noise and I don't want to overreact or bother anyone at work with it. Am I explaining that okay? I hope that answers what you were asking.
How long ago did your husband fall?

Um, it's been about four months now. It happened when we were repairing the porch at home. I guess I've just been feeling this way since then. I mean, four months isn't that long, right? I'm sure it's normal to still be a little jumpy after something like that. I really hope I'm not wasting your time with all this... is four months a normal amount of time to still be bothered by it?
How much of the time do you spend blaming yourself for your husband's fall?

Um, well... I guess I do think about it a fair amount. I mean, I really try not to dwell on it, because I know accidents happen, right? But... yeah, I guess I've just had this really heavy feeling lately. 

It's just this mix of being scared all the time and... and feeling guilty. Like I'm just tense all day long, waiting for the next bad thing to happen. And I can't help but feel like I should have noticed something was wrong with the ladder, or I should have been holding it better. I know I shouldn't beat myself up over it, and I really try to stay positive, but it's just hard to shake that feeling that I should have stopped it from happening. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too sorry for myself.
How often do you think about what you could have done to prevent your husband's fall?

Um, I guess I think about it... a bit. Probably more than I should. I just... I try to push it away because I know it doesn't help anything, but it creeps in. 

I think the hardest part is... well, you know I'm a building inspector, right? So my whole job is noticing things. And I keep thinking that if I missed something at my own house, with my own husband... then maybe I'm just not as careful or competent as I always thought I was. I mean, my work reports are all fine, nobody has said my work is slipping, but... I just can't shake that doubt. I feel like I should be better than that. I hope that's not a silly thing to worry about... do you think it's normal to doubt yourself like that after an accident?
Would you say that this feeling of guilt over your husband's fall is overwhelming at times?

Um, I wouldn't say overwhelming. I mean, it's there, but I don't want to make it sound like I'm falling apart or anything. I still go to work every day and get things done. It's just... sometimes it gets a little heavy, I guess. But I can usually distract myself if I really try. I'm trying really hard to keep things in perspective. That's the right way to handle it, isn't it? Just keep moving forward?
Does this guilt about your husband's fall affect your ability to perform your daily tasks or make decisions?

Um, well, I'm definitely still working. I haven't missed any days or anything, and I think I'm still doing a good job overall. But... I guess I'd be lying if I said it wasn't affecting me at all. 

I've noticed that my inspection reports are taking me a bit longer to finish lately. I just... I catch myself second-guessing things, double-checking everything because I don't want to miss something important again. And, well, I've actually been turning down jobs that involve elevated decks or high porches. I used to do those all the time without even thinking about it, but now I just... I try to pass those on to someone else if I can. 

I know I shouldn't let it affect my work, and I'm really trying to get back to normal. It's just a little bump in the road, right? I mean, it's probably pretty common to be a little extra cautious after something like that happens, don't you think?
Are there any activities or places that you're avoiding because they remind you of your husband's fall?

Um, well, like I mentioned, I have been... sort of avoiding the elevated deck inspections at work. Just the really high ones, you know? I mean, it's not a big deal, my coworkers don't mind taking them. 

And at home... I guess I try not to go out back where it happened. And if my family asks about when I'm going to fix the railing, I usually just change the subject or say I'm too busy right now. I just don't really want to look at it or talk about it yet. But that makes sense, doesn't it? It's pretty normal to want a little space from something like that, right? I'm sure I'll get around to fixing it eventually.
Are there other things besides work inspections and your backyard that you've been avoiding because they remind you of your husband's fall?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I think those are the main things. I'm still doing pretty much everything else the same as always. I still go to the grocery store, I still see my friends, I still drive... all the normal day-to-day stuff. I'm really trying not to let this take over my life, you know? I think I'm doing a pretty good job of keeping things contained. That's a good sign, right? That I'm not avoiding everything?
Do you ever feel like you're reliving the moment of your husband's fall, like it's happening all over again?

Um, well... I guess I wouldn't say I'm completely reliving it, like a movie or anything dramatic. But, um, sometimes at work, if I'm measuring a railing or if I just hear a ladder scrape against the side of a house, I'll get this... flash, I guess? 

Out of nowhere, it's like I can see him falling again, right in front of me. And my stomach just completely drops, and my hands get a little shaky for a minute. But I always catch my breath and get right back to work. I mean, it's just a quick little moment, and then I brush it off. That's probably just my brain processing everything, right? I'm sure it's pretty normal to have little moments like that when you're reminded of an accident, don't you think?
Do you try to avoid thinking or talking about your feelings related to your husband's fall?

Um, well, I guess... I mean, I don't really go out of my way to avoid it or anything. If someone brings it up, I'll talk about it. I just try to stay positive, you know? Focus on the fact that he's okay and recovering. 

I don't really see the point in dwelling on the negative feelings or the scary parts of it. That doesn't really help anyone, does it? I just try to keep a good attitude and keep moving forward. I think it's better to just focus on the good things, right? That's the healthy way to handle it, isn't it?
Would you say that avoiding reminders of your husband's fall is interfering with your daily life or relationships?

Um, well, I wouldn't say it's interfering, exactly. I mean, I'm still working, still getting my job done. I guess... well, maybe my inspection reports are taking just a little bit longer lately? Just because I find myself double-checking things, making sure I didn't miss anything. Which is a good thing for an inspector to do, right? Being thorough? 

And, um, I have been sort of... passing on a few of the jobs that involve elevated decks or porches. Just the really high ones, the ones I used to do all the time. But there's plenty of other work to go around, so it's not a big deal. I'm just being a little more careful with what I take on right now. That makes sense, doesn't it? To ease back into things slowly?
Have you avoided any social activities because they remind you of your husband's fall?

Um, no, not really. I mean, we've never been huge party people anyway, you know? We mostly just hang out with our regular group of friends. 

I guess... well, they did invite us to a barbecue a couple of weeks ago, and they have this really steep, multi-level deck in their backyard. We ended up not going, but that was just because I was feeling a little tired from work. It wasn't really about the deck or anything like that. It's totally fine to just want a quiet night in sometimes, right? I think everyone needs a break from socializing every now and then, don't you?
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I still like doing the things I've always liked doing. 

I guess maybe we haven't been out hiking as much lately, but that's just because the weather's been a little unpredictable, and work has been busy. We still enjoy it, we just haven't had the time. It's normal for hobbies to kind of ebb and flow depending on what else is going on in life, isn't it? I think as long as you're still working and taking care of things, it's okay if you don't have as much time for fun stuff, right?
Have you noticed any changes in your relationships with family or friends since your husband's fall?

Um, no, I don't think so. My husband and I are doing fine. I mean, I try really hard to make sure I'm still being a good wife and supporting him, you know? 

And with my friends... well, we text and everything just like normal. I haven't really noticed any distance or anything like that. I just try to keep things positive when we talk. Nobody wants to be around a downer, right? So I think everything is pretty much exactly the same as it always was. That's a good thing, isn't it? To keep those connections strong?
Have you found that you don't enjoy things as much as you used to since your husband's fall?

Um, no, not really. I mean, like I said, I still enjoy the things I've always enjoyed. 

I guess maybe sometimes I don't get quite as excited about things as I used to, but that's just because I've been working a lot, and, you know, just dealing with everyday life stuff. It's totally normal to not be jumping for joy all the time, right? I think as long as I'm still getting out of bed and going to work and taking care of my husband, that's what really matters. I'm still trying my best to stay positive and appreciate the little things, you know? That's the right way to handle it, don't you think?
Have you felt less interested in things you normally enjoy since your husband's fall?

Oh, um... I think that's kind of what we were just talking about, right? Unless you mean something different? 

But no, honestly, I really haven't lost interest in my usual stuff. Like I was saying, I'm still keeping up with everything just fine. I hope I'm explaining this okay... I know you've asked a couple of different ways now, so I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers. I'm doing this right, aren't I? I really am trying to be as helpful as I can.
Have you noticed yourself participating less in hobbies or activities that you normally enjoy since your husband's fall?

Oh... um, no, not at all. I'm still doing all my normal activities and everything. I still keep busy on the weekends and haven't dropped any of my hobbies or anything like that. 

I... I feel a little bad, because I know this is basically the third time you're asking about this, so I'm really starting to worry I'm not giving you the answer you need, or maybe I'm just not explaining myself well enough? I promise I'm still keeping up with all my routines just like before. It's good to stay busy and keep doing the things you've always done, right? I really do want to make sure I'm being helpful for you... am I doing okay?
